rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` has front matter, so it is a bundled skill and a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement lets a skill put specialized material in linked files. It requires each such link to say when to read the file.

The file has two links to reference files, and each says when to read it:
- `[references/distributed-requirements.md]` comes after "For an obligation that applies separately at each of many sites…". It says to read the file "before drafting it, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`".
- `[references/syntax-details.md]` comes after "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet… or a requirement lives in a nested chapter, read". That states the condition.

The mention of the habeas-evidence skill's `references/fixme.md` is inline code, not a link. It also comes with context: it is where `{fixme}` acknowledgment of a deferred gap is covered. The references to other skills, such as habeas-requirements, are plain names, not links to files.

No violation queries were listed. I found no link that lacks a statement of when to read it, so the site meets the requirement.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
